searchText: https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/#/Config/getDepositContract seems to be the only data structure i can find with an unquoted numeric (chain_id) - is that intentional? I can update our structures if it is, but i had defined it as int64 so that it'd come out as string like all the others... eth2-comply found it (and a few others) 🙂 there's been a few things that have been good with comply, must see if theres plans to take it further to address some of the bits that are less easy heh I'd recommend quoting it - I could have sworn Besu used to treat ChainID as an int and it now uses a `BigInteger` which suggests it can be bigger than a signed long which is bigger than JavaScript will handle accurately as a number (which in turns is why we wound up quoting the uint64 values to start with). Looks like it is treated as a bigint in `go-ethereum`, so yes looks like it should be quoted (think we'll assume that it being no larger than a `uint64` is reasonable) Added a quick PR for it at https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-APIs/pull/114

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/#/Config/getDepositContract seems to be the only data structure i can find with an unquoted numeric (chain_id) - is that intentional? I can update our structures if it is, but i had defined it as int64 so that it'd come out as string like all the others...

excerpts.author: .paulharris
excerpts.content: eth2-comply found it (and a few others) 🙂 there's been a few things that have been good with comply, must see if theres plans to take it further to address some of the bits that are less easy heh

excerpts.author: ajsutton
excerpts.content: I'd recommend quoting it - I could have sworn Besu used to treat ChainID as an int and it now uses a `BigInteger` which suggests it can be bigger than a signed long which is bigger than JavaScript will handle accurately as a number (which in turns is why we wound up quoting the uint64 values to start with).

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Looks like it is treated as a bigint in `go-ethereum`, so yes looks like it should be quoted (think we'll assume that it being no larger than a `uint64` is reasonable)

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Added a quick PR for it at https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-APIs/pull/114
